subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should this issue remain a broad automatic session-artifact garbage-collection tracker, or should the remaining work be narrowed to the existing deleted/reset cleanup path tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/75658 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97103?
rationale: The current implementation space crosses retention policy: deleting stale `.bak.*`, checkpoints, temp files, and archives during normal startup or timers can affect recovery/debug expectations, while the open PR only covers a narrower cleanup-reporting gap.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which stale artifact classes are removed, when, and under which retention settings before accepting a broad proactive cleanup implementation.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting Only
options.body: Treat the open PR as the current fix path for deleted/reset archive reporting and leave broader artifact cleanup for separately evidenced reports.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Keep this issue as a parent and create or reuse narrower trackers for deleted/reset archives, `.bak.*` rotation, temp files, checkpoints, and trajectory artifacts.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which stale artifact classes are removed, when, and under which retention settings before accepting a broad proactive cleanup implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup command and maintenance policy surface that this decision would extend.
